question: What does Article 2(4) of the Charter of the United Nations prohibit?
expected_answer: It prohibits the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of any state.

question: Under Article 13 of the Statute of the International Court of Justice, for how long are members of the Court elected?
expected_answer: For nine years, and they may be re-elected.

question: Under Article 4 of the Charter of the United Nations, which organ recommends admission of a new member and which organ admits it?
expected_answer: Admission is effected by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.

question: Which treaty codifies the general rules on the interpretation of treaties between States?
expected_answer: The Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969).

question: Which article of the Charter of the United Nations makes the International Court of Justice the principal judicial organ of the United Nations?

question: When did the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties enter into force?
State D (illustrative) ratified the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties in 1979. Was it bound by the Convention in 1979?
expected_answer: No; the Convention only entered into force on 1980-01-27, so State D (illustrative) was bound from that date, not from its 1979 ratification.

question: How do the Charter of the United Nations and the Statute of the International Court of Justice relate regarding the Court?
expected_answer: The Charter (Article 92) makes the Statute an integral part of the Charter, and the Statute (Article 1) establishes the Court under the Charter.

question: Has the International Court of Justice treated the prohibition in Article 2(4) of the UN Charter as reflecting customary international law?
expected_answer: Yes; in the Nicaragua case (1986) the Court held that the principle in Article 2(4) also reflects customary international law.

question: Did the International Court of Justice apply the Vienna Convention rules on treaty termination in the Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros case?
expected_answer: Yes; the Court applied the law of treaties, including the rules reflected in the Vienna Convention on termination and material breach.

question: Does Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations preserve the inherent right of self-defence?
expected_answer: Yes; Article 51 preserves the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence if an armed attack occurs.

question: Does signature of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties by State C (illustrative) make it a party?
expected_answer: No; signature alone does not make a state a party.
